claims.text: Melt-spinning can produce an amorphous Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 ribbon.
Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 exhibits a broad solidification range and complex, multistep crystallization behavior.
Both rapid and slow cooling produce extensive primary crystallization in the alloy.
Cooling rate strongly shifts the alloy's transformation temperatures.
At approximately 52 K/s, thermal effects occur near 1291 K and 1206 K, whereas at approximately 3018 K/s they occur near 977 K and 960 K.
Effective use of the proposed intervention requires cooling rates above approximately 3000 K/s.
A nucleation-free supercooled-liquid holding window exists near 980–1000 K in this alloy.
A short isothermal hold in that window immediately after rapid quenching will suppress nucleation of primary non-eutectic phases.
The isothermal hold will facilitate structural relaxation and produce a stabilized, relaxed amorphous configuration.
The relaxed amorphous configuration will be less susceptible to crystallization during subsequent heating.
The proposed hold permits structural relaxation without supplying enough thermal activation to overcome the nucleation barrier of the primary phases.
Structural relaxation during the hold reduces the driving force for nucleation by mitigating undercooling-induced instability.
The proposed thermal cycle will increase the alloy's effective glass-forming ability and thermal stability.
Held samples will retain a larger amorphous fraction than continuously quenched control samples.
Held samples will exhibit a higher crystallization-onset temperature and smaller primary-crystallization exotherms during reheating.
Phosphorus promotes amorphization and modifies the thermal behavior of Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20.

contradictions.description: The material-initial-state field says standard rapid cooling shows extensive primary crystallization, while the baseline says rapid cooling produces an amorphous state. The hypothesis does not clearly distinguish arc-pulse rapid cooling from the faster melt-spinning condition, leaving the stated baseline internally ambiguous.
